correctness.rationale: For each a>=0 the derivative of 0^a splits as h_a+1_S(a)delta_a, where h_a is the indicator of nonempty E_a={0^k1^(a+k): k>=1,a+k in S}; the E_a are pairwise disjoint and disjoint from singleton suffixes {1^j}. Derivatives of 0^a1^b, 1<=b<=a, are delta_(a-b) iff a in S; other derivatives vanish. Unbounded S makes all E_a nonempty and lets every delta_j be generated, giving an isometric closed coordinate-sum c0(N0 disjoint N0). For xi in ell1(words), coefficients A_a=xi(0^a) and B_j=1_S(j)xi(0^j)+sum_{a in S,a>j}xi(0^a1^(a-j)) define bounded Q:ell1(words)->ell1(two indices) with ||Q||<=2, and H=U J Q for the canonical injection J:ell1->c0. J is weakly compact: diagonal coordinate limits of its unit ball stay in ell1 by Fatou, and converge weakly in c0 via its ell1 dual. J is strictly singular: a hypothetical infinite-dimensional isomorphic subspace in c0 gives weakly null unit tail vectors whose inverse under J remains norm-bounded below in ell1, contradicting the Schur property. Noncompactness follows from infinitely many separated q_(0^a) columns. A universal rank-one half-ones approximation and the separation give norm distance exactly 1/2, already known. Independent fresh prefix/suffix tests check 32193 instances on S={2,4}; this is diagnostic, not proof for arbitrary infinite S.
